newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian PM Prodi meets President Scalfaro - official.
newsitem.headline: Italian PM Prodi meets President Scalfaro - official.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi met President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro on Wednesday, Scalfaro's office said in a brief statement.
Earlier, newspapers reported that Prodi was preparing to offer his resignation in a bid to win centre-right backing for a vote on an Italian-led security mission for Albania.
Scalfaro's office said Prodi was accompanied by cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli. It gave no further details. Witnesses said Prodi spent just over an hour in the presidential palace.
Prodi's centre-left government has been thrown into chaos after a hard-left ally, which holds the balance of power in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), refused to back the Albania operation.

The lower house was due to vote on the mission to Albania later on Wednesday, with Prodi now needing the support of the centre-right Freedom Alliance opposition bloc to get approval for the involvement of Italian troops.
Prodi was scheduled to open the debate shortly.
The Freedom Alliance supports the Albania operation, but has refused to vote for the government motion and instead called on Prodi's coalition to accept its own, similar resolution.
It said it might support a joint motion if Prodi promised to tender his resignation.
Scalfaro, who is the supreme arbiter in Italian politics, would almost certainly ask Prodi to seek a vote of confidence in parliament if he offers to resign.
The hard-left Communist Refoundation has indicated it would back the government in such a vote provided it was not tied to the Albania mission, which it sees as a neo-colonialist venture.
Albania was occupied by Fascist Italy 58 years ago this week.
